title: Breadth Sweep

story.briefing: A signal leaves node 0 and spreads outward one link at a time. The Core wants to know how many hops it takes to reach every node, and which nodes it never reaches at all.
story.success: Propagation mapped. The Core knows its own reach.

description: A graph is given as n, the number of nodes numbered 0 to n-1, and edges, an array of [u, v] pairs. Edges are undirected unless stated otherwise, and there are no self-loops or duplicate edges. Starting from node 0, return an array of length n giving the fewest edges needed to reach each node. Node 0 is 0 hops from itself. Use -1 for any node that cannot be reached.

examples.explanation: Node 2 has no links at all.

hints: Working from the edge list directly means searching it every time you need a node neighbours. Build a neighbour list once, first.
Exploring the nearest nodes before the farther ones is what makes the first arrival at a node also the shortest. Handle nodes in the order you discovered them.

Build a neighbour list from the edges. Put node 0 in a queue with distance 0. Repeatedly take the front node and, for each unvisited neighbour, record one more than the current distance and add it to the queue.
